title: Impact of Credit Score Threshold on Loan Default Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)

• Setting: A sharp threshold (minimum credit-score cut-off) determines treatment (loan approval).  
• Assumption: In a narrow neighborhood of the cut-off, borrowers just above and below the threshold are quasi-randomly assigned, so potential outcomes are smooth in the running variable. The only discontinuous jump at the threshold should be treatment status.  
• Key identification assumptions  
  1. Continuity of potential outcomes in credit score around the cut-off.  
  2. No precise manipulation of credit scores right at the threshold.  
  3. Correct functional form / bandwidth choice is used (checked with robustness).  

## 2. R Code
```r
# --- Packages -------------------------------------------------------------
required <- c("readr", "dplyr", "rdrobust")
new_pkgs <- required[!(required %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new_pkgs)) install.packages(new_pkgs, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
lapply(required, library, character.only = TRUE)

# --- 1. Read data ---------------------------------------------------------
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s89_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# --- 2. Define running variable and cut-off -------------------------------
cutoff <- 0.50   # implied by treated == 1 for running_var ≥ 0.5

# --- 3. Main local‐linear RDD estimate -----------------------------------
main_rd <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")
cat("Main RD estimate (local–linear, optimal BW):\n")
print(main_rd$coef["tau.us"])

# --- 4. Robustness checks -------------------------------------------------

# (a) Higher-order polynomial (p = 2)
rd_p2 <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 2, kernel = "triangular")
cat("\nRobustness: 2nd-order polynomial estimate:\n")
print(rd_p2$coef["tau.us"])

# (b) Different fixed bandwidths
for(h in c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20)){
  tmp <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 1, h = h, kernel = "triangular")
  cat("\nBandwidth h =", h, " => estimate:\n")
  print(tmp$coef["tau.us"])
}

# (c) Placebo cut-off at 0.30 (should be ~0 if identification holds)
placebo <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = 0.30, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")
cat("\nPlacebo cut-off (0.30) estimate:\n")
print(placebo$coef["tau.us"])
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Crossing the credit-score threshold is expected to reduce default probability: marginally more credit-worthy borrowers (just above the cut-off) should default less often than those just below. Anticipated sign: negative. Magnitude: roughly −0.08 to −0.12 (an 8–12 percentage-point drop in default likelihood) at the threshold.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The analysis exploits the discontinuity at the credit score threshold to identify the causal effect.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Crossing the credit score threshold increases the default rate.
